To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the unitarity triangle is now well constrained and the CKM picture of quark flavour mixing is consistent with the data, the CKM parameters $\alpha$ and $\gamma$ have been determined with good accuracy and the CP-violating phase $\beta$ is still not very well known, and the SM prediction for the mixing ratio $\xs=\sin^2\beta$ is consistent with experiment.

the unitarity triangle is now very close to a perfect isosceles right triangle with an apex angle $2\beta$ that is consistent with $\beta$ being equal to the Cabibbo angle $\theta_{C}$. The SM prediction for $\xs$ is in excellent agreement with the latest experimental results from LHCb.

(i) the unitarity triangle is still consistent with the SM; (ii) the SM is consistent with the current experimental results; (iii) the SM is in good agreement with the current theoretical predictions; (iv) there is no evidence for physics beyond the SM in the quark flavour sector.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of the parameters of the Cabibbo--Kobayashi--Maskawa quark-mixing matrix $V_{\rm CKM}$, and the implications of the latest experimental and theory results.
the following issues: - the CKM matrix, the unitarity triangle, CP violation and the mixing of $B_s$ mesons in the standard model.
the phenomenological analysis of CP-violating effects in the $B$ system, with particular emphasis on the constraints on the unitarity triangle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SM CKM picture of CP violation is still in good shape.
the unitarity triangle of the CKM matrix is now well determined and that the standard model is consistent with the data.
the CKM matrix is consistent with a unitary matrix, but it does not explain CP violation in $B$ decays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unitarity triangle is almost completely determined, and it is consistent with the SM prediction.
the CKM mechanism of CP-violation is now well established, and that the unitarity of the CKM matrix is confirmed at the 5$\sigma$ level.
the unitarity triangle is still far from being determined.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current experimental data are consistent with the standard model, with the exception of the $B \to D^{(*)} \tau \nu$ decays.
the current experimental and theoretical uncertainties are still too large to allow a meaningful comparison between the SM predictions and the data.
the CKM matrix is still a good fit for the data.
